name: Figma, Inc.

profile.description: Figma is a collaborative, browser-based design platform that pioneered real-time multiplayer design and has expanded into a full product suite spanning FigJam (whiteboarding), Slides, Dev Mode, Sites, Draw, Buzz, and the AI-powered Figma Make and Figma Weave. CEO and co-founder Dylan Field led the company through a failed $20B Adobe acquisition (blocked by regulators) to a successful 2025 IPO. The company serves over 15,900 customers generating $10,000+ in ARR, with Q2 2026 revenue of $370M (up 48% YoY), an 85% gross margin, and 136% net dollar retention, with growth increasingly driven by AI feature monetization via AI credits.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Figma expanded from a single collaborative design tool into a full platform (FigJam, Slides, Dev Mode, Sites, Draw, Buzz, Figma Make) over the past five years, survived a failed $20B Adobe acquisition blocked by regulators, acquired Payload CMS, and completed a successful independent IPO in 2025 — a genuinely transformative period that redefined the company from a design tool into a comprehensive product development platform [1][2]. AI Deployment (2/2): Figma Make (AI design/prototyping) and Figma Weave (AI-powered media generation and editing) are shipping to customers, and management explicitly attributes the FY2026 revenue guidance raise to $1.422-1.428B partly to 'AI credit monetization' and rising paid conversion tied to AI features — quantifiable AI-driven revenue impact [1][3]. Market Share (1/2): Figma remains the dominant collaborative design tool with 15,964 customers over $10K ARR and 136% net dollar retention in Q2 2026, though in the emerging AI-native design tool category, Figma Make faces growing competition from Adobe Firefly and frontier-model-powered tools [1]. Product Pipeline (2/2): Config 2026 unveiled Figma Sites (design-to-publish), Figma Buzz (brand templates), expanded Make and Weave AI capabilities — specific products with launch dates tied directly to the raised revenue guidance [1][3]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Continuous new product launches alongside an 85% non-GAAP gross margin and 79% GAAP gross margin suggest R&D reinvestment well above typical SaaS peer intensity [1].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Figma's mission — 'to make design accessible to all' — is specific, distinctive, and genuinely validated by product decisions: a free tier, browser-based architecture requiring no install, and real-time multiplayer collaboration that democratized professional design tooling away from expensive desktop licenses [4]. CEO Dylan Field's framing at Config 2026 — 'what would you make if you could make anything?' — connects the company's work to a larger creative empowerment purpose. As a company only a decade old and recently public, it lacks the multi-decade track record required for the top tier. Community Impact (1/2): Figma's Net Zero social impact group led the company to sign the Climate Pledge and increased carbon removal/avoidance credit investment 50% to $750,000 — a specific, quantified program, though environmental rather than community-focused [5]. Employee Retention (0/2): No specific tenure or turnover data was identified; CEO Dylan Field has publicly acknowledged the risk of 'messing up our culture while we scale really fast' as an ongoing concern rather than a solved problem. Insider Buying (0/2): CEO Dylan Field has been a consistent net seller — approximately $159.9M in sales over six months with zero purchases and a 10b5-1 plan to sell additional shares, which is common post-IPO but does not signal fresh conviction [6].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock on available metrics. Figma carries almost no leverage (D/E of 4.6%, far under the 70% target, score 1.0) and Q2 2026 revenue grew 48.2% YoY to $370M, comfortably clearing the 10% revenue growth target (score 1.0) [1]. However, profitability metrics floor at zero: TTM net losses produce a profit margin of -123.1% and ROE of -108.6%, both scoring 0.0 against the IOWN floors — driven by massive stock-based compensation expense that masks $867M in TTM free cash flow and $249M in operating cash flow [7]. Forward P/E of 62.7x (on $0.35 forward EPS) exceeds the 60x floor, scoring 0.0, and PEG of 7.95 far exceeds the 3.0 floor, also scoring 0.0 (2x weight) — reflecting an extremely expensive stock relative to near-term earnings. The balance sheet is exceptionally clean ($1.67B cash, $68M debt, ~$1.6B net cash), and daily dollar volume of ~$403M provides maximum liquidity, but the mechanical scoring algorithm penalizes the pre-profitability economics and premium valuation heavily [7].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Figma faces genuine, analyst-flagged structural AI risk — agentic AI-first design tools from frontier model labs could circumvent Figma's collaborative canvas entirely, and CFO Praveer Melwani has publicly acknowledged that rivals' 'ability to train first party models and couple those with their own products is something that we definitely are paying attention to' [8]. At Config 2026, CEO Dylan Field positioned AI as a 'copilot' that removes drudgery rather than replacing creativity, arguing that better AI models strengthen Figma's platform, but the company's ~2% share of the AI design tool category versus Adobe Firefly's ~29% shows Figma is currently behind in the AI-native race it must win to remain relevant long-term. Revenue growth remains strong (48% YoY) and NDR is 136%, so disruption has not yet shown up in results, placing Figma in the EXPOSED tier with an uncertain outcome [1]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Management explicitly cited AI feature adoption and AI credit monetization as drivers behind raising FY2026 revenue guidance twice, most recently to $1.422-1.428B, demonstrating quantifiable AI-driven revenue impact [1][3].

infinite_game.summary: Figma presents a genuine, product-validated mission ('make design accessible to all') and is unusually willing to build AI tools that could cannibalize its own core canvas business rather than defend the status quo — a real signal of existential flexibility. Dylan Field's decade-long tenure and consistent product vision since founding in 2012 build credibility, though the company has not yet been tested by a multi-decade crisis, leadership transition, or sustained growth deceleration. Heavy CEO insider selling tempers confidence that leadership is playing a purely infinite game with this specific stock.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Figma's mission to 'make design accessible to all' is genuinely reflected in concrete product decisions — free tier access, browser-based architecture requiring no expensive desktop licenses, and real-time multiplayer collaboration that changed how design teams work [4]. Dylan Field's Config 2026 framing ('what would you make if you could make anything?') extends this purpose beyond tooling into creative empowerment. As a company only a decade old that IPO'd in 2025, it has not yet demonstrated the multi-decade consistency through crisis and leadership transition that would earn the top tier.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Figma is investing heavily in Figma Make and AI features that its own CFO acknowledges could structurally threaten the core canvas-based business model — building the potential disruptor itself rather than ignoring the threat [8]. The company continues to launch new product lines (Sites, Buzz, Draw) while still deeply unprofitable on a GAAP basis, prioritizing long-term platform expansion over near-term profitability. The abandoned $20B Adobe acquisition was a regulatory outcome rather than a leadership choice, though the subsequent successful independent IPO shows Field committed to the harder path.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Figma's flat organizational structure and transparent culture are emphasized by leadership, with CEO Field publicly engaging with the risks of rapid scaling on culture and investing in executive coaching to grow as a leader [2]. No negative culture indicators were found, but no specific tenure, turnover, or psychological-safety data was identified to support a higher score. The company's 1,886 employees represent a meaningful organization but one still defining its post-IPO cultural identity.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Figma expanded from a single design tool into a broader platform (FigJam, Slides, Dev Mode, Sites) and, more significantly, is actively building AI-native tools (Figma Make, Figma Weave) that its own leadership acknowledges could cannibalize the core collaborative-canvas product that built the company — a genuine willingness to disrupt itself in service of remaining relevant to designers rather than protecting the legacy revenue base [1][3][8].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): CFO Melwani publicly acknowledged the competitive strength of frontier AI-powered design tools rather than dismissing them, explicitly stating the company is 'paying attention to' rivals' first-party model advantages — a clear example of framing competition as a spur for self-improvement rather than a war to win [8]. At Config 2026, the company's messaging positioned AI advances as strengthening rather than threatening its platform, reflecting a learn-from-competition mindset.

investment_thesis: Figma is executing a rare combination for a recently-IPO'd software company: accelerating growth (48% YoY revenue in Q2 2026, up from 41% in Q4 2025) alongside genuine AI monetization through Figma Make and AI credits that has driven FY2026 guidance to $1.422-1.428B [1][3]. Net dollar retention of 136% and 1,635 customers generating over $100K in ARR (+46% YoY) demonstrate that enterprise customers are deepening usage rather than churning despite AI disruption headlines [1]. The balance sheet is exceptionally clean — $1.67B cash against just $68M debt, D/E of only 4.6% — giving Figma ample runway to invest in AI R&D without financing risk. Management's willingness to build Figma Make even though it could cannibalize the core canvas product, and to openly acknowledge rivals' AI model advantages rather than dismiss them, reflects a healthier competitive posture than most incumbents facing disruption [8].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on extreme valuation and unresolved AI disruption risk. At a Forward P/E of 62.7x and PEG of 7.95, the stock prices in sustained hyper-growth that may not materialize — full-year 2026 guidance implies growth decelerating to ~35% at the midpoint, down from 48% in Q2 [1]. TTM net losses produce a -123% profit margin and -109% ROE, driven by stock-based compensation, meaning Figma is years from GAAP profitability even as it generates $867M in free cash flow [7]. The AI disruption risk is real: Figma Make holds only ~2% share of the AI design tool category versus Adobe Firefly's 29%, and frontier AI labs' ability to couple first-party models with agentic design tools could bypass Figma's collaborative canvas entirely — the company's own CFO has acknowledged this threat [8]. CEO Dylan Field has been a large, consistent net seller of stock (~$160M in sales, zero purchases, active 10b5-1 plan), which, while common post-IPO, does not signal fresh insider conviction at current prices [6].
key_catalysts: Continued AI feature monetization (Figma Make, Weave, AI credits) driving further upward revisions to FY2026 guidance beyond the current $1.422-1.428B range, validating that AI is a net growth driver rather than a substitution threat [1][3]

Expansion of the >$100K ARR enterprise cohort (already +46% YoY to 1,635 customers) and sustained 136% net dollar retention, demonstrating durable enterprise lock-in even as AI-native point tools proliferate [1]
Figma Make gaining meaningful share in the AI design tool category from its current ~2% base, closing the gap with Adobe Firefly and neutralizing the structural AI disruption narrative [3]
key_risks: Structural AI disruption risk is real and analyst-flagged: agentic, first-party-model-coupled design tools from frontier labs could bypass Figma's collaborative canvas model entirely, and Figma Make's ~2% category share versus Adobe Firefly's 29% shows Figma is not yet winning the AI-native design race [3][8]

Extreme valuation (Forward P/E 62.7x, PEG 7.95) leaves no margin of safety if growth decelerates faster than FY2026 guidance already implies (~35% full-year vs 48% in Q2), particularly as GAAP losses persist at -123% profit margin [1][7]

Persistent, large-scale CEO insider selling ($160M+ over six months, zero purchases, active 10b5-1 plan for additional shares) removes a potential signal of leadership conviction at current valuation levels [6]
